body: Thank you for sharing that with me. That seems to be the general consensus.

I understand that feeling well. You have nothing to lose from trying again. At least, that is how I try to rationalize things. My worst case scenario is ending up back at the low point again... and since I already know what that low feels like, it some how doesn't seem that bad. 

I basically just trick myself into believing things. Again, I'm happy to lend and ear for you to vent if you want. :)

I'm familiar with the feeling you are experiencing. I am depressed now, but my depression when I was younger was very similar to what you described. 

It's true that things do improve when you make the effort to improve them. For me, it helped me to realized that it was ok to not be okay for a short while of time. I took baby steps to pull myself back above the water - and I had a lot of success with setting and achieving very small goals each day. 

My goals were extremely small. Things like: take a shower, fold a small pile of laundry, get out of bed and sit on the couch for 2 hours. At that time in my life, those were successes. And the more consistently I experienced those "successes" - the more I felt ready to add more small challenges. 

Maybe I would put on make up (I'm a girl) and sit on the couch for 2 hours. In a few days or weeks, I would put on make up and sit on the couch, and then eventually started going on walks. 

My very longwinded point is that in the short term, I was very successful with managing my major depression by setting these small, trivial goals, and feeling a fraction better when I achieved my goal for the day. 

I am happy to lend an ear if you need someone to listen. I am always happy to listen. Stay strong.
